prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence for specific kinds of changes is still thin, as each category has only one completed test so far.
Predictions have consistently been too high compared to measured results.
No clear effect was seen for reordering sign-in steps (sign_in, reorder).
No clear effect was seen for introducing new flows on the home/waiting screen (home, new_flow).
Redesigning the finish step (finish, redesign) significantly hurt performance.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- finish, redesign: -5.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, new_flow: +0.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +1.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, hint] Account Recovery Explanation Banner: Adds a hint on the sign-in screen reassuring users that logging in with their original provider restores their existing pets and data. (why: Support received 8 emails about pets missing or reset after signing in again, making account identity confusing during login.)
1: [adoption, layout] Grid View Pet Selection: Swaps the pet selection screen to a clean grid layout so users can see all available pet options at a glance. (why: Adoption has a low conversion rate of 60.9% and takes a median of 89s, suggesting users take too long browsing pet options.)
2: [home, wait_info] Generation Time Estimate Indicator: Shows explicit estimated time remaining and progress indicator on the waiting screen while pet assets generate. (why: The home/waiting step takes a median of 201s and mean of 2336s, causing uncertainty about whether pet creation stalled.)
3: [adoption, redesign] Preset Pet Selection Cards Redesign: Redesigns the friend choice area with choice cards component featuring distinct visual tags for instant selection. (why: Support recorded 3 emails about custom pet generation failing or looking wrong, making verified preset selection a smoother fallback.)
4: [home, notification] Desktop Ready Notification Toggle: Adds a notification toggle on the waiting screen so users get notified when pet generation finishes. (why: Mean wait time at the home stage is over 38 minutes (2336s), suggesting users wander away while waiting.)
5: [finish, copy] Desktop Controls Explanation Copy: Updates home_intro body copy to explicitly instruct users how to interact, drag, hide, and summon their pet on the desktop. (why: Support received 3 confusion emails specifically asking how to control, hide, or talk to their pet post-onboarding.)

scores.note: Addresses sign-in dropoff with strong support ticket evidence (8 emails); simple banner text addition.
Adoption step has highest dropoff (39.1%) and high duration, though layout change requires a new UI build.
Addresses huge mean duration (2336s) at home step, though previous home flow additions showed weak lift.
Both high adoption dropoff and support emails align, but full card redesign carries UI build cost and moderate redesign risk.
Directly targets high mean wait times where users leave, requiring moderate implementation effort.
Finish step has 35.2% dropoff and support issues; copy updates are low cost and safer than full redesigns.
